issues.description: The last section says docs/07, CONTRACT.md and R10 'are in their own commit' with a stated title, and that `git revert` undoes it. Current repo state: `git log` HEAD is 4aec57a (judge_retest) and no such commit exists. docs/07, CONTRACT.md, docs/05, docs/02, docs/04, gates.yaml and tests/tools/test_checks.py are all uncommitted modifications, and docs/reviews/incr-2.md, check_dogfood.py and gate-dogfood.sh are untracked. The disclosure that the files were changed ahead of approval is honest and adequate. The present-tense claim about the commit is not yet true and should read 'will be'. A one-commit revert would also not isolate the docs/07 and CONTRACT changes unless the other files are kept out of that commit.

The Outcome section says the smoke runs smoke-004 and smoke-006 did not 'beat the baseline on both datasets'. docs/results/treehfd_baseline_first_runs.md says smoke-004 was analytical only, so that statement is vacuous for smoke-004.

The review says the dogfood Evaluator count grows with every `--check` call, so rounds are not the count. .meridian/telemetry.jsonl holds exactly one incr2_review evaluator_verdict (7.4 at 2026-10-02T14:18:31Z), not one per round, although the review lists three rounds (7.4, 7.4, 7.6). The 7.6 verdict is absent from telemetry. `dogfood.sh report` now shows 'pass 5', which is 4 plus 1. The explanation of why the count differs from the rounds does not match the telemetry.

The spend section and the October total ($2.66) cover only model calls in data/ledger. The Evaluator rounds on this review, and on Increments 0 and 1, are model calls that go through no VERA ledger. The review does not state that their cost is excluded or unmeasured. The 'Actual billing was not reconciled' sentence only partly covers this.

In the seeded-fault caveats, the example 'a changed digit in a table ... 5.15 changed to 5.14' is a numeric_prose fault in data/seeded/manifest.csv (run-smoke-006, Results, 'in prose'), not a table fault. The test miss is 'run-smoke-004-b: 100 changed to 105 in prose', consistent with the review's 'configuration number' reading.

The per-stage table and the 110x ratio compare the measured run against the Increment 1 $5.7 estimate. That estimate carries a x2 retry/context margin (docs/reviews/incr-1.md line 322) and assumed about 40 judge questions and 40 audit checks. The review calls the estimate 'worst-case' but does not say that about 2x of the 110x is margin. It also compares GLM and mixed comparison-run costs, which exclude the baseline stage, with whole-run estimates. The review states the second point but not the first.

The JDG-P-01 and T1 reverse-if (1) headline of 97.4% pools 41 real and 36 perturbed items. docs/04 T1 defines the rule 'on the real gate decisions'. The real-only figure (41/41, 95% CI about 91.4-100) is given but not labelled as the rule's literal subject. The real test items are 41 of 77, and 58 of the 77 are one question type, which the review does state.

The Evaluator-round timestamps (rounds 1 and 2 both '14:40:00Z') and the round 1-3 scores could not be checked, because .meridian/evaluator was off limits. Telemetry records only one incr2_review verdict, at 14:18:31Z, which falls before the 14:40:00Z the review gives for rounds 1 and 2. The review's own caveat that the stamps are not real times covers this partly.
